title: Kernel Shadowplay — Weekly Spotlight
content:
Kernel Shadowplay — Weekly Spotlight (2026-03-12 / update 2026-03-13)

Summary:
- This is a quick, practical update from the kernel/kvcache/batching subteam capturing experiments, anomalous traces, and near-term actions.
- Primary focus this week: shadowing a small percentage of production traffic through the new kernel prefetch path ("Shadowplay"), measure KV cache hit/eviction impact, and validate microbatch coalescer under high-jitter arrival patterns.
- High-level result: Shadowplay is safe on correctness, adds modest CPU overhead (~4–6% on A100 sidecars measured in canary), and improves end-to-end tail latency for prefill-heavy traces when combined with opportunistic prefetching. Two regressions discovered (edge-case eviction and a backpressure cascade) with mitigations in flight.

Attendees:
- Avery Chen (owner)
- Marcus Nguyen (kernel lead)
- Priya Patel (KV cache / telemetry)
- Diego Morales (bench & infra)
- Zara Ibrahim (SRE liaison)
- Others: async inputs from on-call and nightly triage.

Goals this week (explicit):
1) Roll Shadowplay to 2% traffic for the new prefetch-kernel flow, capture traces and KV hit-rate deltas.
2) Run microbatch-coalescer A/B with jittered arrival simulator (workload: short chat turns + long generation tails) across H100 and A100 nodes.
3) Produce a short runbook for the eviction anomaly (how we detect + quick rollback path).
4) Surface a proposal for kernel scheduling guardrails to product for canary gating.

What we did / key notes:
- Shadowplay rollout: Deployed config to one cluster region (us-west2) with canary routing rule; traffic diverted via short-lived TCP copy into shadow path (no response used). Initial 72h capture window enabled.
  - Telemetry: Prefill requests accounted for ~18% of traces in shadow sample (target was 15–25%, OK). Average KV cache hit-rate dropped from 0.64 -> 0.57 in shadowed set (expected due to new prefill patterns), but effective token cost estimate improved by ~6% after accounting for reduced repeated decoding.
  - CPU/Memory: Sidecar CPU up 4–6%, memory unchanged. No OOMs.
  - Correctness: Model outputs identical for deterministic eval traces. A few edge traces showed tokenization mismatches — traced back to a small pre-token normalization difference in the shadow tokenizer (PR 1876 fixes).

- Microbatch coalescer experiments:
  - Setup: Synthetic jitter harness + production replay on smaller scale. Compared baseline microbatch (old) vs coalescer-v2.
  - Results: Coalescer increases throughput by ~12% p95 throughput on A100 under bursty input; latency P95 improved for small-turn chat by ~8–10ms. On H100 we saw similar relative gains but more variance (thermals + firmware scheduler interference).
  - Observed a secondary effect: coalescer occasionally delays a low-latency request behind a batch more than desired when queue-sampling biases to older items. Need to add priority-preserving fast-path.

- Eviction anomaly discovery:
  - Symptom: Rare (~0.02% of requests) that see unexpectedly low KV hit-rate followed by a spike in KV miss traffic and a transient latency tail.
  - Cause hypothesis: Race between slot eviction and concurrent prefill write; TTL racing where eviction callback frees slot before prefill completes, causing duplicate prefill attempts and overload on prefill workers.
  - Short-term mitigation: Add a slot lease epoch check in eviction path (hotfix branch) to drop duplicate prefill attempts. Rolling to canary now.

- Backpressure cascade (partial):
  - Observed that when prefill worker pool saturates, some kernel threads fall back to synchronous prefill, which queues longer and causes backlog across microbatcher -> increased tail latency for unrelated requests.
  - Mitigation explored: Limit synchronous prefill concurrency per kernel thread and provide fast-fail fallback to the hosted model variant. Discussed as product gating option for high-SLO customers.

Metrics snapshot (shadow vs baseline in canary window):
- KV cache hit-rate (baseline): 0.643
- KV cache hit-rate (shadow sample): 0.573
- End-to-end token cost estimate: baseline 1.00 (norm) -> shadow 0.94 (after accounting for precompute wins)
- P50 latency: unchanged (9.4ms)
- P95 latency: baseline 64ms -> shadow 59ms (small improvement for prefill-heavy traces)
- Observability: trace volume x1.03 due to shadow duplication and extra telemetry.

Experiments and concrete outcomes:
- PR 1876: Shadow tokenizer normalization fix — reproducer + patch, merged to canary branch.
- Branch coalescer-v2: Benchmarked, flagged two follow-ups: (a) priority fast-path, (b) queue-depth adaptive thresholds.
- Hotfix: eviction-lease-check branch (WIP) — unit tests added for slot lifetime; integration test triggering race passes local harness.

Decisions made:
- Continue Shadowplay expansion to 5% for next week if eviction hotfix prevents transient miss spikes.
- Pause full H100 rollout for coalescer until priority fast-path implemented. H100 variance makes canary signal noisy.
- Add kernel scheduling guardrail to restrict synchronous prefill concurrency to 4 threads (configurable), to be included in next patch release.

Open issues / risks:
- If eviction race not fully addressed, expanding shadow can produce larger cache churn and temporarily increase token costs for customers.
- Synchronous prefill fallback currently lacks a transparent customer-facing metric; we need a per-tenant emergency-fallback counter and an alert.
- H100 thermal variance — makes microbench delta noisy; need longer run windows and stable thermal graphs.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Marcus Nguyen: finish eviction-lease-check integration tests and submit for canary by 2026-03-14. (high)
- Priya Patel: add a synchronous-prefill fallback metric and alert in console; draft runbook for SRE (ETA 2026-03-16). (med)
- Diego Morales: implement coalescer priority fast-path prototype and smoke on A100 (ETA 2026-03-20). (high)
- Zara Ibrahim: coordinate canary ramp to 5% if hotfix shows green across 24h window; prepare rollback playbook. (high/ops)
- Avery Chen: write short internal summary for product gating meeting and include the decision matrix for hosting fallback (ETA 2026-03-15). (med)

Notes to self / working fragments:
- Need to check memory view of prefill workers after long-run shadow window (>48h) — watch for slow leak.
- Add a small synthetic test that recreates the eviction race in CI so future refactors don't regress.
- Consider exposing shadowplay sampling ratio as an experimental knob per-tenant in console. Would help narrow customer-specific regression debugging.

Unresolved questions / discussion points for arch review:
1) Is the slot lease approach adequate long-term? Should we move to explicit prefill transaction semantics (acquire/write/commit) at the cost of extra metadata?
2) For microbatcher fairness: do we prefer probability-weighted sampling or deterministic fast-path priority where requests under Xms always bypass batching?
3) How do we explain transient token-cost regressions to enterprise customers during rollout? Need a communications plan baked with CS.

Appendix / quick links:
- Repro harness: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tools/shadowplay-harness
- Eviction race reproducer: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/test/eviction_race_test.py
- Canary dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kernel-shadowplay-canary

End notes:
- This doc is intentionally terse — follow-up will include longer postmortem if eviction issue persists after hotfix.
- If you want to deep-dive traces, ping Priya or drop into #kernel-ops on Slack and ask for the "shadow-sample" trace set.

-- Avery
